candidates.author: Jeffrey Ip
candidates.subject: refactor(voice): group duplex/connector state and drop dynamic attribute probing
candidates.body:
The duplex run loop tracked the agent utterance across ~24 flat locals with
three near-identical reset blocks, and read its own tuning knobs off the
connector via getattr string probes -- so a typo in a knob name degraded
silently into a default instead of failing. Contracts the duplex loop relies
on (end_of_turn_silence_ms, max_turn_timeout_s, recv_sample_rate,
drain_downlink) are now declared on the connector base class and accessed as
attributes, and the utterance state lives in one object with a single reset.

Also consolidates duplication the refactor exposed: a shared UplinkStream and
iter_downlink helper replace per-connector copies across the websocket,
callback and livekit transports; the websocket's nine wire-dialect parameters
move into a validated schema model behind an unchanged public constructor;
floor control's timer state groups into one object with a single _BARGE_STATES
constant; and the simulator's thirteen voice-only attributes group into a
run object, with tts_cost/stt_cost/voice_config/voice_connector kept as
read-only properties so the public surface is unchanged.

candidates.author: Kevin Messiaen
candidates.subject: fix(hooks): fail open on malformed tool input
candidates.body:
Both hooks crashed with a traceback (exit 1) on unexpected payload shapes:
a non-string file_path raised TypeError at Path(), and a non-dict tool_input
raised AttributeError. Exit 1 means "non-blocking, user-visible", so a
crashing hook neither blocked nor cleanly allowed -- it spammed tracebacks on
every edit while performing no checks, violating the fail-open contract.

Adds explicit isinstance guards on tool_input/file_path/command plus a
top-level catch-all, so future tool-input shape drift cannot wedge the agent.

Also documents that CI typechecks tests while the hook does not: the gap is
intentional and one-directional, so the hook never blocks what CI would pass.

* test: extract shared zstd test helpers to test_helpers/zstd.py

read_raw_compressed_entry out of test_zipfile_multiframe.py so the

* fix: handle multi-frame zstd in async ZIP read path

A single zstandard decompressobj only spans one frame; on eof it
rejects further input. The previous ZstdDecompressor crashed with
'cannot use a decompressobj multiple times' on the second chunk of
any multi-frame entry -- exactly the entries PR #3746's writer
produces for samples whose JSON exceeds 200 MiB.

inside ZstdDecompressor: track a _pending buffer for unused_data
carryover and replace the inner decompressobj on every frame boundary.

Adds an integration test through AsyncZipReader that monkey-patches
the per-frame cap to 64 KiB so the round-trip is fast (<1s).

candidates.subject: Rename the samples-listing errors_only param to an extensible filter enum
candidates.body:
`GET /evals/{id}/samples` now takes `filter=errors` instead of the
boolean `errors_only=true`, so future listing filters are one new enum
member rather than an accumulation of boolean params. The value is
typed as a Literal end to end; an unrecognized filter is rejected (422)
rather than silently answered with the full listing, and the CLI trusts
the server-filtered result — the client-side fallback filter (and the
`select` hook it required) is removed. Skew with a server from an older
install is not defended: the server runs locally from the same install
as the CLI in all but upgraded-mid-eval cases.

candidates.author: Eric Winsor
candidates.subject: Prevent math scorer from executing model output (#4361)
candidates.body:
* Prevent math scorer from executing answer text

`math()` currently passes normalized model output to SymPy `parse_expr()`.
That compiles and evaluates the string with Python builtins, so an ordinary
model answer can execute arbitrary code on the evaluator host during scoring.

Parse answers and targets as data with a pinned mathematical grammar and a
strict plain-expression AST. Bound extraction and symbolic work, run parsing
and comparison in cancellable worker processes, and keep model rejection
incorrect while invalid targets are unscored.

* Harden math scorer parser boundaries

The LaTeX dependency can mis-score percentages under supported ANTLR 4.11 runtimes and perform some expensive SymPy operations before Inspect applies its structural limits. Abrupt worker exits also surface without enough scorer context.

Normalize percentages before dependency parsing, constrain and validate supported ANTLR runtimes, keep binomial and gamma construction symbolic, and reject remaining eager operations before parsing. Preserve worker exits as scorer errors while identifying whether they occurred during target parsing or answer scoring.

* Remove residual math parser evaluation paths

candidates.subject: feat(models): add cross-platform onnxruntime-genai backend + refactor winml (#3960)
candidates.body:
* feat(models): add cross-platform onnxruntime-genai backend + refactor winml

Add a cross-platform `onnxruntime-genai` backend that runs ONNX LLMs exported
by the ONNX Runtime GenAI Model Builder on CPU/CUDA/DirectML/WebGPU/AMD-NPU via
the `og.Config` provider API. All lm-eval logic (single-pass log-likelihood,
multiple-choice, rolling perplexity, generation) lives in
`ONNXRuntimeGenAILM(TemplateLM)`, following the `OptimumLM(HFLM)` single-file
subclass precedent.

Refactor `winml` into a thin `WindowsML(ONNXRuntimeGenAILM)` subclass that
overrides only execution-provider selection, inheriting the shared scoring
core. This removes the previous winml quality debt: the per-token
teacher-forcing loop (now a single `get_output("logits")` pass), the direct
`loglikelihood` override that bypassed `TemplateLM` token handling, and the
silent `(0.0, False)`-on-exception path that corrupted scores.

Add a shared parametrized test suite (unit tests for the scoring math with a
fake `_forward_logits`, plus CPU smoke tests over hellaswag/wikitext/gsm8k
using a tiny Model Builder fixture), packaging extra, and docs. The test is
